title: The Lost Ones
author: Mia Sheridan
about: An escaped convict, Duke Caraway, returns to his poor Appalachian hometown to hunt the real killer of a woman he was convicted of murdering, a crime he cannot remember. Only Winsome Fair, a guidance counselor he rescued as a child, believes he is innocent. Together they uncover a network of stolen children and corrupt officials.
bio: Mia Sheridan. Her publisher lists this book as from the author of All the Little Raindrops. A full biography is coming soon.
why: A romantic suspense novel set in Appalachia, from the author of All the Little Raindrops.

title: Icy Control
author: Carly Robyn
bio: Carly Robyn. Her other books include Ice Ice Baby and Fire and Ice. A full biography is coming soon.
why: A Boston Bobcats novel, as shown on the cover.

title: The Witch
author: Freida McFadden
about: After losing her job and apartment, Julia Barlow moves into Pemberton, her family's 17th-century estate in rural Massachusetts, to care for her grandmother. The house turns hostile: a clock stops at the same hour each night, lights flicker and a voice calls for help. As she digs into the estate's past, she learns of a woman executed for witchcraft in 1692 and uncovers family secrets.
bio: Freida McFadden is a physician based in Boston and the author of The Housemaid. Her publisher says her novels have sold over 90 million copies and been translated into more than 45 languages.
why: A standalone thriller told across two timelines, 1692 and the present day.

title: State of Terror
author: Hillary Rodham Clinton & Louise Penny
about: After a new president appoints a political rival, Ellen Adams, as secretary of state, a series of apparent terrorist attacks begins. They turn out to be part of a larger international plot involving Pakistan, Afghanistan, Iran, nuclear weapons development, the Russian mob and a rogue terrorist group. Adams, a young Foreign Service officer and a journalist work to uncover and stop the conspiracy.
bio: Hillary Rodham Clinton was the 67th U.S. secretary of state. Louise Penny is a multiple award-winning, number one New York Times bestselling novelist.
why: An instant number one New York Times bestseller, co-written by a former U.S. secretary of state and a bestselling crime novelist.

title: 1% Lifesteal 5
author: Robert Blaise
about: After an attack by Nahar, imperial investigators want to question Freddy, which takes him out of the Northern Belt to Starhold, a frontier city on the Empire's front line. There he keeps proving his worth through arena fights, university, front-line duty and dungeons, while facing who he has become.
bio: Robert Blaise. A full biography is coming soon.
why: Book 5 of the six-book 1% Lifesteal LitRPG series.

title: Murder Mystery Advent Calendar: The Killer Checked In
author: M. L. Winterquill
about: An interactive Christmas murder-mystery challenge for adults built around the Kingsmoor hotel. The premise invites readers to work through 24 clues, consider 9,600 suspects and identify the one killer. It is presented as an advent-calendar-style mystery experience rather than a conventional novel.
bio: The listing credits M. L. Winterquill. The available public listing does not provide a verified author biography, so Book Heaven is keeping this section factual rather than guessing about the writer.
why: A seasonal, interactive mystery format that turns the countdown to Christmas into a clue-solving challenge.

title: Darkness of Dragons: A Graphic Novel
author: Tui T. Sutherland & Mike Holmes
about: Qibli knows the ancient dragon Darkstalker must be stopped. He believes he might be able to change the future with the power of Darkstalker's scroll, but the prophecies are difficult to rewrite. Using the small animus objects he has borrowed from Turtle, Qibli must decide whether he can become the magical force Pyrrhia needs—or risk bringing disaster to Jade Mountain, his friends and his family. This is the tenth Wings of Fire graphic-novel adaptation, illustrated by Mike Holmes.
bio: Tui T. Sutherland is the author of the Wings of Fire series. Mike Holmes illustrates this graphic-novel adaptation, bringing the dragon characters and Pyrrhia's world to the page.
why: The tenth graphic-novel adaptation in the bestselling Wings of Fire fantasy series, continuing Qibli's story in illustrated form.

title: The Naughty List Agreement
author: Katherine Garbera
about: Cora Quill, the Queen of Christmas, needs a new toy maker after her supplier is caught up in a scandal. The only person who can help is Nick Bari—the grumpy toymaker she fired years earlier. Nick is also the current Santa Claus, and he must find a wife before Christmas Eve to keep the holiday season alive. Their festive deal brings two stubborn people together, with Christmas magic, rivalry and romance along the way.
bio: Katherine Garbera is a USA Today bestselling author of more than 145 novels. Her romances are known for big emotions, humour, twists and happily-ever-after endings. She lives in Kent, England.
why: A Christmas advent romance told in daily chapters, pairing a toy maker with the Queen of Christmas in a festive enemies-to-lovers story.

title: The Collateral Heart
author: Jeffery Deaver
about: A devastating arson in Manhattan leaves a building destroyed and a trail of clues that may reveal where the arsonist will strike next. Forensic criminalist Lincoln Rhyme and detective Amelia Sachs investigate, turning to a popular history podcaster for help. Their case intersects with Long Island detective Desdemona Vale, who is searching for the killer of a young woman from her neighbourhood. As the investigations converge, the team must uncover the suspect's larger plan before more lives are lost.
bio: Jeffery Deaver is an internationally bestselling thriller writer and the creator of the Lincoln Rhyme series. He has written more than forty novels, and his work has been translated into numerous languages and published around the world.
why: The seventeenth Lincoln Rhyme novel, bringing the forensic-crime team back for a case involving arson, coded clues and intertwined investigations.

title: Strangers on the Mountain
author: A. J. Rivers
about: When a woman is attacked outside a bar, FBI agent Aurora Gray is called to investigate. The main suspect disappears into the mountains, where his burned-out camper and body are later found. As more missing men and victims emerge, Aurora discovers that each man was hiding a troubled past—and that someone may be offering desperate people a way to disappear and start over. The apparent escape could be a deadly trap, and Aurora must find the person hunting them before another victim vanishes.
bio: A. J. Rivers writes mystery and thriller fiction, often combining suspense, crime investigations and unexpected twists. Her author biography describes a lifelong interest in mysteries and crime-solving stories, with inspiration drawn from researching true crime.
why: Book five in the Aurora Gray FBI Mystery Thriller series, taking the investigation into a remote mountain setting.

title: The Wrong Daughter
author: Dandy Smith
about: Sixteen years after ten-year-old Olivia disappears from her bedroom, her family is stunned when a woman claiming to be Olivia returns. Her younger sister Caitlin remembers the night differently and is unsure whether the woman is really her sister. As both women keep secrets and memories fail to match, the family must face the possibility that welcoming the wrong daughter home could destroy them all.
bio: Dandy Smith is a bestselling psychological-thriller author. She studied Creative Writing at Bath Spa University, completing both undergraduate and master's degrees. Her novels have been published internationally and translated into several languages; she lives in Somerset, England.
why: A twist-filled psychological suspense novel about a missing child, a sister's return and the secrets a family has kept for sixteen years.

title: Growing Up Pentecostal: A Memoir
author: Phil Matarese
about: Growing Up Pentecostal: A Memoir explores Phil Matarese's childhood in a Pentecostal environment, the spiritual questions that followed him into adulthood, and the way his understanding of faith developed over time. Phil recalls spontaneous church services, later experiences in more structured Christian settings, and the moment visits from high-school friends made him see his familiar church through a different perspective.
bio: Phil Matarese is the author of Growing Up Pentecostal: A Memoir. In writing it, he waited until he felt able to approach his experiences with honesty, balance and respect. He made careful choices to protect the privacy of others, including changing names and leaving out stories that were too personal to share.
why: The memoir invites readers to examine what they believe and why, learn about other faith traditions, and remain open to thoughtful dialogue without mocking or dismissing the people and communities that shaped them.

title: He Who Fights with Monsters: Book Eight
author: Shirtaloon (Travis Deverell)
bio: Shirtaloon (Travis Deverell). A full biography is coming soon.
why: Book Eight of the He Who Fights with Monsters series, published by Aethon Books.

title: The Good Daughter
author: Karin Slaughter
about: Charlie Quinn has grown up in the shadow of a home attack that killed her mother and fractured her family, and she has become a lawyer like her father, a well-known defense attorney in Pikeville. When a violent tragedy traumatizes the town and she becomes the first witness on the scene, long-suppressed memories resurface and the truth about the original crime threatens to come out.
bio: Karin Slaughter. A full biography is coming soon. Her other books include Pretty Girls, The Kept Woman and Pieces of Her.
why: An instant New York Times bestseller, adapted as a Peacock limited series starring Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy.

title: Journey to Joy: March–September 1872
author: Ginny Dye
about: Set in 1872, this installment follows several characters as the country keeps changing. Anthony and Carrie are pulled onto an unexpected path after a theft, Annie works to bring hope to children who have none, and Elizabeth and Peter marry in Boston. The story also touches on the ongoing struggle to build a country that includes everyone.
bio: Ginny Dye is described as a best-selling author who is passionate about bringing history to life through historical fiction.
why: Book 18 of the Bregdan Chronicles, an inspirational historical fiction series.

title: Beyond What Is Given
author: Rebecca Yarros
about: Lt. Grayson Masters is focused on finishing Apache helicopter training when his new roommate, Sam Fitzgerald, gets under his skin. Sam, recently expelled from college, pushes him to open up while hiding secrets of her own. Their growing attraction becomes complicated when Sam learns that another woman once held a place in Grayson's heart.
bio: Rebecca Yarros is a bestselling author of more than twenty novels, including Fourth Wing and In the Likely Event. Her work has earned the British Book Award for Book of the Year and the American Library Association's Alex Award. She lives in Colorado and co-founded the nonprofit One October in 2019, which supports children in the foster system.
why: Book 3 of 5 in the Flight & Glory series, a military romance.
